title: Uterine Leiomyosarcoma (uLMS) & Endometrial Stromal Sarcoma (ESS): Stanford Criteria, Morcellation Risk and Systemic Regimens
subject: ss-gynaecological-oncology
refs: Berek & Hacker's Gynecologic Oncology 7th Edition Ch 14
DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology 11th Edition Ch 84
NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Uterine Sarcoma (Version 1.2024)

steps.say: Uterine leiomyosarcoma is an aggressive mesenchymal malignancy characterized by specific diagnostic histological hallmarks that differentiate it from benign cellular leiomyomas.
steps.tx: Diagnosis of uterine leiomyosarcoma (**uLMS**) relies upon the Bell and **Stanford criteria** triad: severe diffuse cytological atypia, geographic **coagulative tumor necrosis** (tumor cell necrosis), and an elevated mitotic index demonstrating **>=10 mitoses per 10 HPFs**, distinguishing sarcoma from benign leiomyoma variants.

steps.say: Unlike endometrial adenocarcinoma which uses endometrial depth and cervical spread, uterine leiomyosarcoma staging is determined by absolute tumor dimension and anatomical boundaries.
steps.tx: Dedicated **sarcoma FIGO staging** employs a **5 cm cutoff** to establish early local extent: **Stage IA <=5 cm** and **Stage IB >5 cm** in largest tumor diameter. Stage II denotes pelvic extension, Stage III indicates intra-abdominal dissemination, and Stage IV signifies mucosal invasion of the bladder, rectum, or distant hematogenous metastases.

rows: Tumor limited to uterus, <= 5 cm greatest dimension
Early localized disease; favorable local control
Tumor limited to uterus, > 5 cm greatest dimension
Large localized primary; higher recurrence risk
Tumor extends beyond uterus within the pelvis
Invades bladder/rectal mucosa or distant organs (lungs)

steps.say: The unintentional power morcellation of an unsuspected uterine leiomyosarcoma during minimally invasive fibroid surgery represents a severe surgical error that disseminates malignant tissue.
steps.tx: Elective intracorporeal **uterine morcellation hazard** causes widespread peritoneal dissemination of sarcoma cells, transforming localized disease into diffuse abdominopelvic carcinosarcomatosis. Morcellation causes severe **iatrogenic dissemination**, leading to an alarming **survival reduction 73% to 46%** in 5-year overall survival across prospective oncology registries.

left.title: Intact Specimen Extraction
points: Extracted intact via minilaparotomy or protected endobag
Peritoneal cavity protected from cellular spillage
5-year overall survival in Stage I uLMS reaches ~73%

right.title: Uncontained Power Morcellation
points: Spreads viable malignant mesenchymal fragments across peritoneum

steps.say: The standard primary surgical therapy for patients suspected of having uterine leiomyosarcoma is en bloc total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral adnexectomy.
steps.tx: Standard operative management requires en bloc **TAH-BSO**. Routine **omission of lymphadenectomy** is accepted clinical practice because occult **nodal metastasis <3-5%** in apparent early-stage uLMS; lymph node dissection does not confer overall survival benefits and is reserved for clinically or radiologically enlarged suspicious nodes.

nodes.label: Perform complete midline laparotomy with careful exploration
Execute total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy
Avoid morcellation and maintain tumor pseudocapsule intact
Omit routine systematic lymphadenectomy unless nodes are clinically enlarged

steps.say: Low-grade endometrial stromal sarcoma represents an indolent hormone-sensitive uterine neoplasm defined by characteristic genetic translocations and intense sex hormone receptor expression.
steps.tx: In **LG-ESS**, neoplastic stromal cells recapitulate proliferative-phase endometrial stroma. The tumor is driven by recurrent **t(7;17) translocation** producing the **JAZF1-SUZ12 fusion** oncogene, displays diffuse **ER/PR positivity**, runs an indolent clinical course, and demonstrates a propensity for **late recurrence** even decades after initial resection.

rows: Typically negative for ER and PR
Bland uniform cells resembling proliferative stroma
Marked pleomorphism with necrosis and brisk mitoses

steps.say: High-grade endometrial stromal sarcoma is an aggressive mesenchymal malignancy characterized by distinct cytogenetic alterations and loss of hormonal receptor expression.
steps.tx: Conversely, **HG-ESS** is characterized by the distinct **t(10;17) translocation** generating the **YWHAE-NUTM2 fusion** transcript. Microscopically it exhibits round-cell morphology with brisk mitoses, is **ER/PR negative**, pursues an **aggressive course**, and fails to respond to endocrine manipulation, requiring cytotoxic systemic chemotherapy.

left.title: LG-ESS Biology & Behavior
points: Intense estrogen and progesterone receptor expression
Slow growth, high response to aromatase inhibitors

right.title: HG-ESS Biology & Behavior
points: Loss of hormone receptors (ER and PR negative)
Aggressive haematogenous dissemination; cytotoxic chemotherapy required

steps.say: For patients presenting with unresectable, metastatic, or recurrent uterine leiomyosarcoma, systemic cytotoxic combination chemotherapy represents the mainstay of palliative treatment.
steps.tx: In metastatic or recurrent uLMS, standard **first-line uLMS chemo** consists of combination **gemcitabine docetaxel** or single-agent **doxorubicin**, achieving objective clinical **response rate 25-35%**; trabectedin, dacarbazine, and the multikinase inhibitor pazopanib represent validated second-line systemic treatment options. Multidisciplinary tumour board review ensures optimal clinical staging and coordinates tailored surgical oncological interventions.

nodes.label: Diagnose advanced, metastatic, or recurrent uterine leiomyosarcoma
Administer first-line gemcitabine plus docetaxel or doxorubicin
Assess tumor response by RECIST 1.1 on surveillance CT imaging
Initiate second-line targeted therapy with pazopanib or trabectedin upon progression

steps.say: Given the intense hormone dependency of low-grade endometrial stromal sarcoma, endocrine manipulation provides prolonged disease control in adjuvant and metastatic settings.
steps.tx: Maintenance **hormonal therapy in LG-ESS** utilizes **aromatase inhibitors** (letrozole or anastrozole) or high-dose progestins (megestrol acetate). Conversely, there is an absolute **contraindication to tamoxifen/estrogen** because tamoxifen acts as a partial uterine agonist and stimulates lethal tumor progression in these estrogen-dependent neoplasms.
